eligibility.quote:
We're seeing occasional failures in [test_subscription__rmw_cyclonedds_cpp::take_sequence](https://github.com/ros2/rmw_implementation/blob/master/test_rmw_implementation/test/test_subscription.cpp#L526) ... #1  0x0000ffff81ca9d68 in __GI_abort () at abort.c:79
#2  0x0000ffff81af782c in sertype_rmw_realloc_samples (ptrs=0xaaaaca346c10, d=0xaaaaca027250, old=0x0, oldcount=0, count=1)
    at /home/ubuntu/ros2_ws/src/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/rmw_cyclonedds_cpp/src/serdata.cpp:458

failed_conditions.quote:
As it stands, the take_sequence test fulfills the first part of that
(it was initialized by rmw_message_sequence_init()), but doesn't fulfill
the second part (populated by ROS messages).  In certain situations,
this could lead to an aborted test later on.

loudness.quote: In most cases, the sequence of bytes stored in that pointer is *not* zero, so we never end up trying to call `ddsi_sertype_realloc_samples` (and hence we don't `abort()`).

resolution.quote:
I think not: from the changes in this PR I suspect I misread the `rmw_take_sequence` interface and the sequence of messages passed in actually conforms to what Cyclone DDS expects (an initialised array of pointers to messages), and https://github.com/ros2/rmw_implementation/pull/175 seems to clarify that.

That makes this one incorrect and the problem it tried to address a non-existent problem.
